newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - July 31.
newsitem.headline: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - July 31.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:
* Eagle Mining Ltd A$2.52 (+0.07)
* Great Central Mines A$2.80 (+0.10)

Eagle Mine is seen as next on Barrick Gold Corp's takeover list after Joe Gutnick's Great Central Mines, The Australian reported. Barrick again refused to confirm or deny overnight that it was planning a takeover bid for Great Central after foreign exchange dealers said a Canadian corporate bought A$450 million on Tuesday night.
* Equatorial Mining Ltd A$0.23 (unch)

Directors of the Chilean/Australian El Tesoro copper project have ordered a feasibility study based on a production target of 75,000 tonnes of copper a year, up from 60,000 tonnes a year, said Equatorial Mining, a 39 percent owner.
* General Property Trust A$2.68 (+0.04)

GPT announced its first half results early on Tuesday, posting a 63 percent rise in net profit to A$110.9 million and a slightly higher distribution of 10.4 cents per unit. It also forecast a 9.3 cent distribution in the second half.
* Westfield America Trust A$1.24 (+0.04)
Westfield is expected to release its first half results just before the start of trade.
* Foster's Brewing Group Ltd A$2.62 (-0.03)

Newspapers reported that the Molson Cos Ltd had said in its annual report it wanted to buy out Foster's 40 percent stake in Molson Breweries Ltd. Also overnight, Molson Breweries said the National Hockey League had rejected Molson's latest offer for Canadian broadcast rights. Molson had held the rights since 1985.
* James Hardie Industries Ltd A$4.42 (+0.04)
James Hardie told its shareholders at its annual meeting in Melbourne it saw a significantly higher profit in the current year to March 31, 1998.
* Davids Ltd A$1.00 (-0.11)
Grocery wholesaler and retailer Davids Ltd said late on Wednesday its pre-abnormals full year profit would be substantially below analysts' forecasts of about A$48 million.
"It's down substantially from that," new chief executive officer Don Bourke told Reuters. "The bottom line is that the profit hasn't been satisfactory in the second half of the year," Bourke added.
* Wattyl Ltd A$6.74 (-0.01)

Paint manufacturer Wattyl Ltd managing director Greg Boshell said on Wednesday a profit increase in the year to June 30, 1998 was achievable, despite a subdued outlook for its main market Australia. "We are looking for a profit increase and we think that is achievable," Boshell told Reuters in a telephone interview.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
